sections.title: What it really costs
sections.intro: Monthly running costs, how the fees compare, and the one-off costs of buying.

items.head: Repair fund ¥18,200/month = ¥235/m²
items.detail: MLIT guideline for a building like this (under 20 floors, floor area < 5,000 m², floor area estimated ~3,400 m²): average ¥335/m², ⅔ of buildings ¥235–430. At the guideline average this flat would pay ≈ ¥25,932/month (+¥7,732). A fund below the guideline usually means future increases or a one-off levy (一時金).
items.cmp: Peers built ±5 years (226 watchlist condos): median ¥200/m², middle half ¥170–244 → this flat is at the 69th percentile.
items.ask: Please share the 長期修繕計画 and the current repair-fund balance. Are increases or a 一時金 planned?

items.head: Management fee ¥10,000/month = ¥129/m² (委託(通勤))
items.detail: Small buildings cost more per flat; staffed (常駐) management costs more than visiting (巡回).
items.cmp: Peers of similar age and size (0–60 units): median ¥116/m² → 57th percentile (70 condos)

items.head: ≈ ¥78,447/month before parking and property tax
items.detail: Loan ¥50,247 (100% of price, 35 years, 1.00% variable — the Apartments tab default) + fees ¥28,200
items.ask: What was the last 固定資産税・都市計画税 bill for this unit?

items.head: One-off buying costs ≈ ¥1,187,400–¥1,543,400
items.detail: Agent fee (仲介手数料, 3% + ¥60k + tax) ¥653,400 · plus registration tax and scrivener, loan fees and guarantee, fire + earthquake insurance, stamp duty, pro-rated property tax and fees: typically 3–5% of the price. Budget for renovation separately.

sections.title: Earthquake safety

items.head: Built 1972 — old seismic standard (旧耐震)
items.detail: Designed before June 1981. Many such buildings are fine, but loans, tax credit and resale are harder unless retrofitted.
items.ask: Has a 耐震診断 been done? Results and any retrofit (耐震改修) plans?

items.head: Structure: SRC, 8 floors
items.detail: RC/SRC are the norm for condos.

items.head: 30-year chance of shaking ≥ 6-lower here: 70% (≥ 6-upper: 21%)
items.detail: ≥ 5-upper: 99%. Modern buildings are designed for this; the risk is contents, lifts, pipes and the days without water or power.
items.cmp: Study areas (population-weighted, ≥ 6-lower): median 59%, range 24–89% → rank 59 of 78 from the safest

items.head: Ground: 埋立地 — shaking amplified ×1.72
items.detail: Soft ground amplifies shaking (AVS30 212 m/s; about 1.6 or more counts as soft). Ask how the building is founded (piles to bearing stratum?).
items.ask: What kind of foundation does the building have (支持層までの杭基礎)?

src: J-SHIS 地震ハザードステーション

sections.title: Water and ground
sections.intro: Depth bands are the maximum assumed scenario (想定最大規模) at SUUMO's map point; SUUMO's point is approximate, so the worst value within ~100 m is shown too.

items.head: River flood: none at the point (up to < 0.5 m nearby)
items.detail: The flat is on floor 1: it could be flooded, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Storm surge: 0.5–3 m at the point (up to 3 m or more nearby)
items.detail: The flat is on floor 1: it could be flooded, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Liquefaction tendency: high
items.detail: Landform: 盛土地･埋立地 on 旧水部 (国土地理院). Condo towers on piles usually stand, but roads, pipes, gas and sewers around them can fail for weeks (as in Urayasu 2011).
items.ask: Was the building or site damaged in 2011 (東日本大震災)? Ground improvement?

items.head: Area context (Chiba Mihama)
items.cmp: 95% of residents live in some water zone · 97% on high-liquefaction ground · 0.5% in landslide zones

items.head: Old maps
items.detail: Check what the site was before (sea, paddy, river) on 今昔マップ; past disaster records and 大規模盛土 maps come with the MLIT API key.

sections.title: Energy, windows and running cost
sections.intro: Energy labels are only required for new buildings (from April 2024): used flats almost never show them, so proxies are used.

items.head: No energy label (normal for used flats)
items.ask: Is there a 住宅性能評価書, BELS or 長期優良住宅 certificate?

items.head: Likely designed to before the first insulation rules (1980)
items.detail: Era is only a hint: condos were not required to meet the energy standard until 2025.

items.head: Window type not stated
items.detail: In condos the window frames are common property: you usually cannot replace them yourself; inner windows (内窓) are allowed and subsidised.
items.ask: Are the windows single or double glazed? Were sashes replaced in a major repair?

items.head: Gas type not stated
items.detail: Propane (LPG) costs much more than city gas.
items.ask: City gas or propane? Electricity contract (high-voltage bulk 一括受電)?

items.head: Mortgage tax credit: check eligibility
items.detail: Built before 1982: needs a 耐震基準適合証明書 · registered area ≥ 50 m² ✓. Without an energy certificate a used home falls in the basic tier: 0.7% of the loan balance up to ¥20M for 10 years (max ¥140k/year). With a 省エネ基準適合 certificate it is 13 years; ZEH-level / 長期優良 raises the cap to ¥35M.
